description:
User ruling 2026-11-18 (relayed by Make Distiller Fast, verbatim: "delegate the map building, slicing, struct field work to the Optimize agent"). Builder: Optimize. Source: MDF distiller profile at develop 2eff1dec2 (bench, sample 1 ms for 2 s from 0.4 s in, 1,498 samples of a 2.84 s run, inclusive shares, one run; raw: bench distill-hunt/prof.j.base.txt).

fz_struct_get_field_ref = 3.4% (51), from JSON object_key / object_value / array_item: a struct field read through a call that re-validates the word. With a known slot it is a load at the field's offset. A recipe row (fz_struct_get_field_ref(word, slot)) in the recipe table (fz-sc8.213, #727), same shape as fz_struct_schema_id_ref.

Not in scope: the wider recipe-row follow-up (float arithmetic, integer division, remaining word readers), which awaits the user.

comments.text: Cannot be built as a recipe row as written (Optimize, 2026-11-18): the answer depends on the field kind byte, whose place fz_struct_get_field_ref(process, word, field_offset) finds via the schema registry (Schema::value_field_kind_offset); a recipe sees only its arguments. After that the read is ~8 branch-free instructions. Missing: the tuple field count at the read (SlotLayout { fields }.kind_offset(index); Prim::TupleField(Var, u32) carries only the index; the three emitters have the count at hand). Proposed (awaiting the user): Prim::TupleField carries the field count; the runtime function takes (word, index, count) and places the kind byte by SlotLayout with no registry lookup; then a real recipe row with a parity proof. Touches interp, JIT, AOT and the IR printer. JSON-object probe (80-byte object, 50,074 instr/decode at a3edb6f32 + #739): fz_struct_get_field_ref 5.2% inclusive.

Concordant evidence 2026-11-18 (Make Distiller Fast, bench profile at 37c5473cd, read off disassembly). Heap::read_struct_field_ref is 3.4% self. On every field read it bumps a borrow counter, bounds-checks a table, then scans the struct's field descriptors linearly (0x28-byte stride) comparing ids to find the field. Callers: JSON decoder object_key/object_value. Same design question as decision 76 (Prim::TupleField carries the field count).

title: A struct field read at a known slot is one load
